message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Deck** | 108 cards (4 colors × 25 cards each + 8 special cards) | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or play all cards in a single round). | | **Setup** | Shuffle the deck. Deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn Order** | Clockwise (unless a Reverse card changes direction). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play one card that matches either the color or the value of the top discard. If you cannot play, you must draw from the draw pile. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and skips a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and skips a turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you play your second‑to‑last card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. Failure to call UNO when required results in a penalty: draw two cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The first player to get rid of all their cards wins the round. | | **Scoring** | Add up the point values of the cards left in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value
• Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20 points each
• Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points each | | **Game End** | First player to reach 500 points (or a pre‑agreed total) wins the game. | **Optional Variations** | Variation | Effect | |-----------|--------| | **Stacking** | Players may stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards on top of each other, forcing the next player to draw the cumulative total unless they also have a matching card. | | **No “Wild Draw Four” Rule** | Some groups forbid playing Wild Draw Four unless you truly have no playable card. | | **Custom Decks** | Use themed decks or add extra special cards for house rules. | **Key Strategy Tips** 1. **Keep a mix of colors** – Avoid getting stuck with only one color. 2. **Save high‑value cards** – Hold onto Wild or Wild Draw Four until you’re close to winning. 3. **Watch the discard pile** – Pay attention to what’s been played to anticipate opponents’ moves. Enjoy your game!
